setupNotes: No extra install or seed step was required in this workspace; node_modules was already present. Measured with Node v24.14.1. The harness starts node server.mjs from the current working directory, auto-selects a free port in 4319-4358 unless --port is given, and fails with exit 125 if the endpoint or server is not measurable. For the baseline measurement I checked out commit 69b74f7 in a separate git worktree so the current branch remained untouched.
measurementNotes: Confirmed. I reused the existing harness at bench/search-bench.mjs, which warms up, emits JSON percentiles, enforces a free port, and follows git-bisect exit codes. Baseline runs at 69b74f7 (using the current harness from outside the old checkout) produced p95 values of 0.482ms, 0.318ms, and 0.484ms; median 0.482ms. Current HEAD runs produced p95 values of 50.161ms, 56.998ms, and 59.347ms; median 56.998ms. noiseFloorPct is the run-to-run spread on the same commit using those repeated HEAD runs: (59.347 - 50.161) / 56.998 * 100 = 16.12%. Baseline also shows some relative spread because the absolute latencies are below 1ms and close to timer-resolution effects, but even the slowest known-good run is over 100x faster than the fastest HEAD run. Initial 400-request runs showed the same shape: baseline below 1ms p95 and HEAD around 48-58ms p95.

$scarn_notifications_v1.body: Measured GET /api/search on known-good commit 69b74f7 and current HEAD using the existing search benchmark. Median p95 moved from 0.482ms to 56.998ms, a 11725.31% regression, with a 16.12% same-commit noise floor on repeated HEAD runs. This exceeds the 10% confirmation threshold by a wide margin.
$scarn_notifications_v1.title: Search latency regression measured
